{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development, Hosting and Revenue-Share Agreement with HDI)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Scope:** Verified playbook findings only. We represent the Company (Customer); HDI is the vendor.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings**: 6 compliant, 8 deviations and 5 missing clauses. The dominant theme is **omission rather than aggressive drafting** — this is a short revenue-share site deal in which HDI bears all design, development, hosting and maintenance cost and is paid solely out of a 30% share of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor, and the drafting reflects that informality.

The most significant gaps are the total absence of five protections we would normally treat as non-negotiable for a vendor that builds, hosts and operates a customer-facing site and holds our Content, user information and order data: **no HDI performance warranty**, **no indemnity (including no IP-infringement indemnity)**, **no limitation of liability**, **no IP ownership or assignment provision**, **no insurance covenant**, and **no transition assistance or data-return mechanic on exit**. As drafted, we have no contractual claim to the Site or the deliverables HDI builds for us, no defence if a third party asserts infringement, unlimited mutual damages exposure, and no right to get our data back.

On the economics, the **Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment** (one-half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is our principal commercial objection: it is payable on *any* Company termination — including a termination for HDI's breach — is one-way (Section 4.2(b) relieves HDI of any reciprocal payment), and scales without limit as the Site succeeds, materially exceeding the playbook's three-month fee ceiling. We have proposed capping it rather than deleting it, given HDI's cost-bearing role.

Several items we would ordinarily expect to fight are **already acceptable and are not redlined**: New York governing law (Section 10.5), no MFN, no minimum purchase or volume commitment (fees are pure revenue share), no employee non-solicit binding us, and the Section 6.1 non-compete, which sits at the playbook fallback (term-only, no post-term tail, bounded to Deerskin Products on a single online channel, with closeout and Joan Cook carve-outs, against a two-year post-term restraint on HDI in Section 6.3).

**Note on one finding:** the AUDIT finding (HDI's Section 3.4 inspection right) failed automated verification and should be re-confirmed manually before it is put to HDI. It is shown separately in Section 3 below and excluded from our headline asks.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 6.1 (with § 6.2, § 6.3, § 1.1) | Term-only restraint, no post-term tail, single-channel and Deerskin-Products scope, closeout carve-outs. Only the internal-development/acquisition carve-out is absent — noted, not redlined. |
| 2 | High | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 9 (Warranties) | Warranties limited to corporate existence, authority, enforceability, no-conflict. No professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-law or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Fails the fallback. Proposed new Section 9(c). No "AS IS" disclaimer present. |
| 3 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 10.5 | New York law, conflicts disapplied; no arbitration and no foreign seat. Only the express exclusive-venue designation is missing — noted for information, no redline. |
| 4 | Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | No clause (cf. § 1.1–§ 1.3, § 2.1, § 5.2, § 8.1, § 10.2) | No ownership or assignment provision anywhere; the only express IP grant runs from us to HDI (§ 6.1). Proposed new Section 5.5 confirming Company ownership of Content, Site, deliverables and Site data, with HDI licence-back and no joint ownership. |
| 5 | Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Missing** | No clause (cf. § 9, § 10) | No cap, no consequential-damages exclusion. Unlimited mutual exposure. Proposed mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Section 3 fees and USD 1,000,000, with standard uncapped carve-outs and our § 3 / § 4.2 payment obligations excluded. |
| 6 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | No clause (cf. § 3.1–§ 3.4) | No parity or price-matching obligation in either direction. Fees are a flat 30% revenue share. § 6.1 is exclusivity, addressed under that rule. |
| 7 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 3.1–§ 3.4 | No minimum, guaranteed volume or take-or-pay; the $11,000 monthly floor operates in our favour. § 4.2 exit cost assessed under LD/T4C, not double-flagged. |
| 8 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | No clause (cf. § 10.2) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binding the Company. Matches preferred position. |
| 9 | Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 10.3 | Bare successors-and-assigns clause; no consent standard, so HDI could transfer the engagement (and access to our data and site) to a competitor. Not walk-away — no block on our assignment and no HDI termination/re-pricing on our change of control. Minimal edit proposed. |
| 10 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away territory)** | § 6.1 (cf. § 4.1, § 1.6, § 4.2, § 6.3) | Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit; any Company termination triggers the Termination Payment. We take the fallback rather than deletion, given § 6.3 restrains HDI for term plus two years: cap at 12 months and auto-terminate on HDI launch/service failure. |
| 11 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing (walk-away territory)** | No clause (cf. § 1.1–§ 1.4, § 9, § 10, § 10.7) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language at all; no IP-infringement indemnity from the party that builds, hosts and operates the Site. Proposed new Section 9(c) with notice/control/cooperation and a Company-Content carve-out. No reciprocal Company indemnity to narrow. |
| 12 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away territory)** | No clause (cf. § 1.1–§ 1.3, § 8.1, § 10) | No insurance covenant for a hosting vendor holding our user information and data. Proposed new Section 10.9 at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' comp, certificates on request); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M flagged in comment. No coverage tail sought. |
| 13 | Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 4.2(a) (cf. § 3.1, § 4.1) | Termination Payment of one-half of trailing 12-month Net Sales above $800,000 exceeds three months' fees once annual Net Sales pass roughly $0.9m and grows without limit; payable even on our termination for HDI's breach. Cap at three months' fees proposed; deletion offered as preferred alternative. |
| 14 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 1.4 | Sole inbound grant runs to "the Company" only; no affiliate or contractor coverage and no mechanism to add them, failing the fallback. Not expressly revocable, and § 10.3 largely covers successor transfer. One-sentence extension proposed. |
| 15 | Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.1 | Evergreen one-year renewals (acceptable) but a 90-day non-renewal notice window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling, just short of walk-away. Seek 30 days (60 days acceptable). No renewal uplift language, so the price cap point is not engaged. |
| 16 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 4.1, § 4.2(a)–(b) (cf. § 1.6, § 1.2, § 1.3) | The 90-day mutual convenience right sits at the fallback; the failure is the exit penalty. One-way Termination Payment, several times three months' fees at $2M annual Net Sales, biting even on termination for HDI's breach. Cap at three months' fees and disapply where we terminate under § 1.6 or for HDI's breach. |
| 17 | Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | No clause (cf. § 4, § 8, § 10.7, § 1.4, § 2.1, § 8.1) | No exit assistance and no obligation to return our Content, user information or customer data. Proposed new Section 4.3: up to 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. |

---

## 3. Finding requiring manual re-verification (not yet an ask)

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Verification | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation (asserted) | § 3.4 (cf. § 8.2) | **Failed** | Finding records that HDI's inspection right meets or beats the preferred position on notice (30 days' prior written notice), timing (our normal business hours) and cost (HDI bears its own costs unconditionally), and is scope-limited to the General Manager's payment-calculation records, but contains no frequency limit, permitting unlimited repeat inspections. Proposed a once-per-twelve-month cap. **This finding did not pass verification and should be confirmed against the executed text before we raise it.** |

---

## 4. Walk-away items

The following findings were assessed as falling into walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN, missing).** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and supplies the software and Content administration tools under Sections 1.1–1.4, yet there is no defence or indemnity of any kind — most critically no IP-infringement indemnity. We should not host our brand and customer channel on a platform we have no right to be defended on.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE, missing).** HDI hosts the Site on its own server and holds our Content, user information and data (Sections 1.1–1.3, 8.1). A hosting vendor processing personal data with no insurance is the playbook's express walk-away scenario, and it compounds item 1 — an uninsured, unindemnified counterparty.
3. **Full-term exclusivity with no performance exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 6.1).** Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term, with Section 1.6 permitting termination only for a missed initial launch and any other Company termination triggering the Section 4.2 payment. We are locked to HDI's channel irrespective of how HDI performs. Given Section 6.3's reciprocal two-year restraint on HDI, we have proposed the fallback (12-month cap, automatic termination on HDI launch or service failure) rather than deletion.

**Closely related and, in practice, part of the same walk-away conversation:** the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment (LD and T4C). It is one-way, uncapped in growth, and payable even where we terminate for HDI's breach — which is precisely what makes the exclusivity in item 3 inescapable. Items 3 and 4.2(a) should be negotiated together.

**Also material, though not classified as walk-away:** the missing IP ownership provision (we have no contractual claim to the Site or deliverables), the missing limitation of liability (unlimited mutual exposure), the absent HDI performance warranty, and the missing transition and data-return mechanic (our data could be stranded or deleted on exit).

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Confirm commercial appetite on the two linked economics issues** — the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment cap (three months' Section 3.1 fees, with disapplication where we terminate under Section 1.6 or for HDI's breach) and the Section 6.1 exclusivity fallback (12-month cap plus automatic termination on HDI service or delivery failure). These are our lead asks and should be tabled as a package.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the five inserted provisions — new Section 9(c) (HDI performance warranty), new Section 9(c) (HDI defence and indemnity), the mutual limitation of liability, new Section 5.5 (ownership), new Section 10.9 (insurance) and new Section 4.3 (transition assistance and data return) — together with the minimal edits to Sections 1.4 (affiliates and contractors), 4.1 (30-day non-renewal notice) and 10.3 (assignment consent).
3. **Re-verify the Section 3.4 audit finding** manually against the executed text. If the absence of a frequency limit is confirmed, add the once-per-twelve-month cap to the redline; if not, drop it.
4. **Confirm insurance positioning with risk management** — we have pitched at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M) and should know in advance whether the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback is acceptable, given HDI's data access.
5. **Prepare the trade narrative.** HDI bears all design, development, hosting and maintenance cost under Sections 1.2 and 1.3 and is paid solely from revenue share. We should be explicit that we are not seeking to disturb that bargain — hence the capped rather than deleted Termination Payment and the fallback rather than deletion on exclusivity — but that risk allocation (warranty, indemnity, insurance, liability cap, ownership, data return) is not part of the price and must be papered.
6. **Do not raise** the compliant items — Section 6.1 non-compete, Section 10.5 governing law, MFN, minimum commitment and non-solicit. Where useful in negotiation, Sections 6.3 and 3.1 (the $11,000 floor) can be cited as terms already running in our favour.

*Prepared solely from the verified findings supplied. Section references are taken from those findings; no conclusion has been drawn beyond them.*"}
